title: Associative owner-chain current-generation boundary
mode: Generated local ASCII/Binary DXF fast slice

implementation.change: Associative owner-chain scanning now uses only the DICTIONARY callback range and unique Named Object Dictionary callback from the current import generation.
implementation.failurePrevented: A DICTIONARY retained in dx_data from an earlier import can no longer supply missing current-generation ownership/membership evidence and make a current associative record appear rooted.
implementation.boundedness: Prior dictionary list entries traversed to reach the current range are capped at kMaxAssociativeOwnerNodes; current nodes and edges keep their existing caps.
implementation.compatibility: No DRW_Interface virtual, codec wire format, serializer qualification, or strict-output policy changed.

generatedRegression.shape: First import retains a dictionary/NOD graph whose edges would complete a later associative owner chain. Separate second-import controls omit the current dictionary or NOD while retaining a current associative action; another probe duplicates the current NOD callback.
assertions: Capture, handle-code scan, and owner-chain scan complete.
Current-generation dictionary range is [1,1), excluding the prior dictionary.
The associative record is retained but zero owner chains and zero qualified records are reported.
The following DICTIONARYVAR sentinel is delivered.
A stale NOD does not substitute for a missing current NOD callback.
Duplicate current NOD callbacks mark root identity ambiguous and owner-chain completion false.

assessment.commitLimitation: .git is read-only in the shared workspace; source, test, plan, and receipt edits remain uncommitted.

limitations: This closes only the per-import provenance boundary of generic owner-chain evidence. It does not classify associative group-code roles, establish class-specific reference closure, enable replay, or qualify constraint semantics or support claims.
